meta.document: The Larkin House Rules and Resident Policies

contact.frontDesk: Attended lobby, 24 hours. Reachable in person, through the resident app, or at the leasing line during office hours.
contact.residentManager: Live-in resident manager, office on the lobby level, Monday through Friday 9:00am - 5:00pm.

meta.sourceOfTruthNote: This file is the source of truth for building policy. Figures here are authoritative and should be quoted exactly. Do not paraphrase a number, and do not invent a policy that is not in this file; if it is not here, say so and offer the resident manager.

answerRules.note: Rents and availability live in the inventory feed, never here. Any request for an accommodation, any question about whether a specific person qualifies, and any dispute goes to the resident manager with full context.

legalReview.scope: The regulatory status of the building and everything that follows from it were corrected on 2026-09-07. The file had described the market-rate residences as free-market and not stabilized, which is wrong under RPTL 421-a(16), and it had carried a forfeitable hold deposit, a non-refundable pet fee, move-in and move-out deposits, amenity deposits, and a two-month early termination fee that New York does not permit. Counsel reviews the stabilization language in leaseTerms.regulatoryStatus, the renewal mechanics, and the removal of each of those charges before any of it is quoted to a caller.
legalReview.interim: Until counsel signs off, the leasing team escalates every rent stabilization, renewal increase, and lease termination question to the resident manager instead of answering it. The derived knowledge article for lease terms is held out of the published set for the same reason.

pets.weightLimitNote: Fifty pounds applies to each pet at full grown weight, not to the two of them combined. Two 50-pound dogs are fine.
speciesAllowed: Small caged animals such as rabbits, guinea pigs, and hamsters
speciesProhibited: Any animal prohibited by the NYC Health Code Article 161
pets.petFeeNote: There is no pet fee. General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(a) caps everything an owner may hold to one month's rent as security, and Real Property Law 238-a bars fees outside a short enumerated list, so a non-refundable charge for a pet is not permitted here. Damage a pet causes is repaired and billed at cost after the fact, with photographs and an itemized statement, the same as any other damage.
pets.depositNote: There is no pet deposit, no pet fee, and no monthly pet rent. General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(a) is the reason those charges do not exist, not a justification for them: it caps the total an owner may hold to one month's rent, and Real Property Law 238-a does not list a pet charge among the fees an owner may collect. Pet damage is billed as documented damage after the fact.
pets.restrictedBreedBasis: The list comes from the building's general liability carrier, not from a house preference. It does not apply to service animals or approved assistance animals.
registrationDocuments: Veterinarian record showing breed, age, and adult weight
NYC dog license number, required by NYC Health Code Article 161 for every dog over four months old
Proof that your renters insurance liability coverage does not exclude the breed
pets.registrationTiming: Pets are registered at lease signing, or within 5 days of the pet arriving if you get one mid-lease. An unregistered pet is a lease violation, not a fee.
pets.leashRule: Dogs are leashed in the lobby, the elevators, the corridors, and every amenity floor. The only place a dog is off leash is inside The Green.
pets.elevatorRule: Dogs ride the passenger elevators. If someone at the door would rather wait for the next car, let them.
pets.wasteRule: Waste is picked up immediately, indoors and out, and goes in the bag station at the gate of The Green or in a hallway chute closet bin, never in a lobby trash can.
pets.petSpaAccess: The Pet Spa on three is included with your fob. Book a 45-minute slot in the resident app, one dog per session, up to 7 days out. Closed Wednesdays 9:00am to 11:00am. Outside groomers are not permitted to work in the room.

dogRunRules.name: The Green
dogRunRules.hours: Daily 6:00am - 11:00pm, closed 7:00am - 7:30am while it is hosed down
rules: Your dog stays in your sight the whole time you are in the run
No food, no treats, no toys left behind
Dogs in heat and dogs under four months stay out
Two dogs per resident at a time
No guest dogs, and no dog walkers with a group from outside the building
Pick up after your dog and use the bag station at the gate

pets.serviceAndAssistanceAnimals: Service animals and qualifying emotional support animals are not pets. They are exempt from the pet fee, the two-pet limit, the weight limit, and the breed list under the Fair Housing Act and the New York State and City Human Rights Laws. Requests are handled by the resident manager, never over the phone by the leasing team.
pets.visitingPets: A guest's dog may visit for up to 3 nights and has to be announced at the front desk. Visiting dogs cannot use The Green or the Pet Spa.
pets.petWalkersAndSitters: Dog walkers and sitters are added to your recurring visitor list at the front desk with a photo ID on file. They get lobby and elevator access to your floor only, and only on the days you list.
pets.noiseAndNuisance: A dog that barks for long stretches while you are out is handled the way any noise complaint is handled: a note from the resident manager, then a written notice, then a notice to cure.
pets.violations: First incident is a written notice. A second within six months is $100. A third is a notice to cure the lease. An unregistered pet, a restricted breed, or a bite incident goes straight to the resident manager.
pets.nycNotes: New York City's pet law, Administrative Code 27-2009.1, waives a no-pet clause when a pet is kept openly for three months and the landlord does nothing. The Larkin allows pets, so the clause is moot here, but it is the reason we register pets promptly rather than looking the other way.
pets.residentSummary: Two pets per residence, fifty pounds each, dogs and cats. There is no pet fee, no pet deposit, and no monthly pet rent — New York does not permit them, and damage a pet causes is billed at cost after the fact instead. Register the pet at signing with a rabies certificate, a vet record, and the NYC dog license, and check the restricted breed list before you fall in love with a puppy. Your fob opens the Pet Spa on three and The Green on four, and dogs stay leashed everywhere else in the building. Service animals and approved emotional support animals are not pets under the law. They pay no fee, the breed and weight limits do not apply, and the resident manager handles those requests directly.

parking.hours: 24 hours, attended. Between midnight and 6:00am, call the booth about 20 minutes ahead so your car is at the door when you are.
parking.rateStructure: One flat rate. There is no premium for a larger space and no discount for a compact car.

evCharging.cost: Included in the $425. There is no separate charging fee and no idle fee.
evCharging.assignment: EV spaces are assigned to residents with an electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle, in the order they ask. All twelve are spoken for right now and there are 5 households waiting.

parking.licenseAgreement: Parking runs on a month-to-month license, separate from your lease. Thirty days' written notice ends it from either side. Giving up the space means going back to the end of the waitlist.

waitlist.order: Strictly by the date you asked. Residents come before applicants, and an applicant can join the list once a lease is signed.
waitlist.howToJoin: Ask the front desk or email residents@thelarkinlic.com. There is no fee to hold a place.

guestParking.hours: Guest vehicles are accepted 6:00am - 11:00pm, subject to space that day. The booth cannot hold a spot in advance.
guestParking.billing: Charged to your resident ledger, not paid at the booth.

requirements: Vehicle registration in the name of a resident on the lease
A key left with the booth, since the garage is attended and cars are stacked
parking.sizeLimits: Clearance is 6 feet 8 inches. Vehicles longer than 18 feet are $75 a month more and are subject to space.
prohibited: Long-term storage of a vehicle you do not drive
Storing anything in the space other than the vehicle

bicycles.room: The Bike Room on three, 220 tagged spaces, free
bicycles.allowance: One space per residence at no charge, a second on a waitlist that is running about a month
bicycles.access: 24 hours by fob, from the service elevator. Tags are issued by the resident manager Monday through Friday 9:00am - 5:00pm.
bicycles.rules: Tagged bikes only. Untagged bikes are removed after a 14-day notice on the frame. Bikes do not ride the passenger elevators or live in hallways, and e-bike batteries are not charged in the room or in the residence per FDNY rules.

parking.streetAndAlternatives: There is metered and alternate-side street parking on 46th Avenue and 5th Street, and a Citi Bike dock at 46th Avenue and Vernon Boulevard. Most residents here do not keep a car.
parking.residentSummary: The garage is 84 attended spaces under the building, entered from 5th Street, staffed around the clock. A space is $425 a month on a license that runs month to month with thirty days' notice, and twelve of the spaces have Level 2 charging at no extra cost. There is a waitlist right now of about two months, 19 households deep, ordered by the day you asked. Guests park for $45 a day when there is room, motorcycles are $195, and the bike room on three is free with one tagged space per residence.

overnightGuests.beyondThat: Someone staying longer than that is an occupant, not a guest, and needs to be added to the lease. Adding an occupant is free and takes a short form and a photo ID.

guests.roommateLaw: New York Real Property Law 235-f lets you live with your immediate family and one additional occupant plus that occupant's dependent children, whether or not they are on the lease. Tell the resident manager within 30 days so the person gets a fob and shows up on the access list.
guests.registration: Register a guest in the resident app or with the front desk. Unannounced visitors are held in the lobby while the desk calls you. The desk logs a photo ID for anyone going upstairs without you.
guests.visitorPass: The resident app issues a QR visitor pass good for 24 hours. It opens the lobby vestibule and the elevator to your floor only. Passes are not issued to a guest for a stay longer than 3 nights — at that point the person is added to your recurring visitor list.
guests.recurringVisitors: Housekeepers, dog walkers, sitters, and home health aides go on a recurring visitor list at the desk with a photo ID and the days they come.
guests.escortRule: Guests are your responsibility from the moment they walk in. You are liable for what a guest does to the building.

amenityGuestRules.general: A guest in any amenity space is accompanied by you the entire time. No amenity is available to a guest on their own, ever.
amenityGuestRules.theWorks: Two guests per residence, accompanied, and each signs the waiver at the front desk once per lease year. Under 16 is not permitted on the fitness floor.
amenityGuestRules.theStudio: Residents only. No guests, including in the open hours between classes.
amenityGuestRules.theRecoverySuite: One guest per booking. An outside massage therapist or trainer counts as your guest, has to be licensed in New York, and files a certificate of insurance before the appointment.
amenityGuestRules.theTerraceAndPool: Two guests per residence at the pool, signed in at the front desk. Children under 14 are with an adult in the water. The deck is the same two-guest rule during quiet hours after 10:00pm.
amenityGuestRules.theLarder: The room seats twelve including you, so eleven guests.
amenityGuestRules.thePlayroom: Twenty-five people in the room at once counting adults. A child under twelve has an adult with them.
amenityGuestRules.theScreeningRoom: Eighteen seats, so seventeen guests plus you.
amenityGuestRules.theOverlook: Sixty-five people including residents, per the fire occupancy posted at the door. Private events run Friday, Saturday, and Sunday 6:00pm - 11:00pm, with a certificate of insurance for any event with catering or bar service. There is no event deposit. Cleaning or damage beyond normal use is billed at cost after the event, with photographs and an itemized statement. The sky terrace stays open to other residents even during a private event.
amenityGuestRules.theStudy: Six guests in a conference room. The lounge itself is for residents.

guests.partiesAndEvents: Gatherings above ten people belong in a reserved amenity space, not in a residence. Amplified music is not permitted in outdoor amenity space at any hour.
prohibited: Handing your fob to a guest
Propping any door, including the stair doors and the garage pedestrian door
Sending a guest to an amenity floor to wait for you
guests.shortTermRentalCrossReference: A paying guest is not a guest. See the subletting and short-term rental policy.
guests.residentSummary: Guests are welcome and they are yours to escort. Fourteen consecutive nights is the limit, and thirty nights in any six months, after which the person is an occupant and gets added to the lease at no cost. Register anyone coming up in the resident app or at the desk, and use the app's 24-hour QR pass rather than handing over your fob. In the amenity spaces a guest is with you the whole time: two at the pool, two in The Works, none in The Studio or The Green, and sixty-five people total in The Overlook.

moving.howToReserve: Book the freight elevator through the resident manager, in person or at residents@thelarkinlic.com, at least 5 business days ahead. The slot is confirmed in writing.
moving.blockLength: Four-hour blocks. A second block the same day is available if nobody else has it.
moving.permittedHours: Monday through Saturday, 9:00am - 5:00pm. No moves on Sundays and no moves on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, or Christmas Day.
moving.entrance: Service entrance on 5th Street, into the freight car. Nothing moves through the lobby.

deposit.note: There is no move-in deposit and no move-out deposit. General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(a) caps everything the owner may hold to the one-month security deposit, so the building does not take a separate advance to let you move.
deposit.damage: The resident manager walks and photographs the corridor, the freight car, and the loading area before your block starts and again when it ends. Damage from your move is repaired and billed at cost afterward, with the photographs and an itemized statement.

moving.feeNote: There is no move fee and no move deposit. Your mover's certificate of insurance is what stands behind damage during the move; anything past it is billed at cost after the work is done, never collected up front.

certificateOfInsurance.certificateHolder: 5-08 46th Avenue Owner LLC, c/o Halbrook Residential Management, 5-08 46th Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101
certificateOfInsurance.note: No certificate, no elevator. This is the single most common reason a move gets pushed a day, so send it early. Licensed movers issue these routinely; ask your mover for a COI naming both entities above.

moving.protection: Building staff hang the elevator pads and lay masonite on the corridor and lobby-level path before your block starts. Do not move the pads.
moving.selfMoves: You can move yourself, and the same reservation, hours, and deposit apply. A self-move still needs a COI only if you hire anyone with a truck; a rented van you drive yourself does not.
moving.furnitureDeliveries: A delivery that ties up the freight car for more than 30 minutes is treated as a move: reserve the block, same hours. Anything smaller goes through the service entrance during business hours with the desk notified.
moving.largeItems: Nothing goes up the stairs. The freight car is 4 feet 6 inches wide, 7 feet 8 inches deep, and 8 feet high, with a 4,000-pound capacity. Measure a sofa before you buy it.
moving.contractorsAndInstallers: Anyone doing work in a residence — cable installers, closet companies, art hangers, movers — files the same certificate of insurance and works Monday through Friday 9:00am - 5:00pm.
moving.moveOutNotice: Sixty days' written notice before your lease ends, and the move-out block booked the same way as the move-in.
moving.residentSummary: Reserve the freight elevator through the resident manager at least five business days out, in four-hour blocks, Monday through Saturday 9:00am to 5:00pm — no Sundays and no building holidays. Your mover sends a certificate of insurance five business days ahead naming 5-08 46th Avenue Owner LLC and Halbrook Residential Management as additional insureds, with a million per occurrence and statutory workers comp. There is no move fee and no move deposit. The resident manager photographs the corridor, the freight car, and the loading area before and after your block, and damage from a move is repaired and billed at cost with an itemized statement. Everything comes in through the service entrance on 5th Street, and staff hang the pads and lay the floor protection before your block starts.

trashAndRecycling.chuteRoom: A chute closet on every residential floor, floors 5 through 33, next to the service elevator. Your fob opens it.
trashAndRecycling.chuteHours: The trash chute is open 6:00am - 11:00pm. The closet itself is open 24 hours, so recycling and compost can go down any time.
chuteRules: Household trash only, in a tied bag under 15 pounds
No glass down the chute — it breaks and it carries through the whole stack
No cardboard, no hangers, no construction debris
Nothing left on the floor of the closet

streams: Blue bin: metal, glass, plastic, and cartons
Green bin: paper and flattened cardboard
recycling.location: Both bins are in the chute closet on your floor
recycling.cardboard: Broken down flat. A box left whole fills the bin for the entire floor.
recycling.collection: Porters bring the floors down nightly. DSNY collects recycling on Tuesday and Friday mornings.

compost.bin: Brown bin in the chute closet, lined, emptied nightly
compost.accepted: Food scraps, food-soiled paper, and plant waste. Compostable bags are stocked in the closet.
compost.basis: New York City requires residential organics separation citywide, and DSNY has been issuing fines to buildings since April 2025 — $100 for a first violation, $200 for a second, $400 after that. The building eats those fines, so the brown bin is not optional.
compost.collection: Collected with recycling, Tuesday and Friday mornings.

bulkItems.process: Get a tag from the front desk, then bring the item to the bulk staging room on the cellar level, 8:00am - 8:00pm. Do not leave anything in a hallway or a chute closet.
bulkItems.collection: DSNY takes bulk on Tuesday mornings.
bulkItems.mattresses: Sealed in a plastic mattress bag before it leaves your residence. DSNY fines $100 for an unbagged mattress and the fine follows the residence. Bags are $10 at the front desk.
bulkItems.hallwayFeeNote: Anything left in a corridor, a stairwell, or a chute closet is removed by staff at $75 per item, charged to your ledger.
bulkItems.constructionDebris: Not accepted. If you are having work done, the contractor carts it out.

electronicsAndHazardous.eWaste: Electronics cannot go in the trash in New York State. The building runs an e-waste collection in the cellar the first Saturday of every quarter, 9:00am - 1:00pm, with a licensed recycler.
electronicsAndHazardous.batteriesAndBulbs: A collection bin sits next to the mail room for household batteries and CFL bulbs.
electronicsAndHazardous.lithiumBatteries: Damaged or swollen e-bike and scooter batteries go to the front desk, not in any bin. FDNY rules, and it matters.
electronicsAndHazardous.paintAndChemicals: Not accepted anywhere in the building. DSNY runs SAFE disposal events across Queens.

trashAndRecycling.textiles: A refashionNYC bin in the cellar takes clothing, shoes, and linens year-round.
trashAndRecycling.residentSummary: There is a chute closet on every residential floor next to the service elevator, and your fob opens it. Household trash goes down the chute between 6:00am and 11:00pm in a tied bag — no glass, no cardboard. The blue and green recycling bins and the brown compost bin are in the same closet and are open around the clock, and the compost bin is a city requirement, not a house preference. Bulk items get a tag from the front desk and go to the staging room on the cellar level, mattresses have to be bagged first, and anything left in a hallway is removed at $75 an item.

includedInRent: Cooling from the building's four-pipe system
Amenity access, including The Works, The Study, and the bike room
WiFi in every amenity space and the lobby
paidSeparately: Electricity, through Con Edison, in your name
Internet and television in your residence
Parking, storage, and any optional service

heatAndCooling.system: Four-pipe fan coil, individually zoned, with a thermostat in the living area and in each bedroom
heatAndCooling.note: Heating and cooling both come off the building's central plant, so you set the temperature and it does not show up on a bill. New York City requires heat from October 1 through May 31 at 68 degrees during the day and 62 at night; the building runs warmer than that.
heatAndCooling.seasonalChangeover: The plant changes over between heating and cooling in April and again in October. There are a few days each spring and fall when only one is available, and the resident manager posts the dates.

electricity.accountRequired: In your name, active on your lease start date. Open it at least 3 business days before key pickup — the front desk cannot release keys without the account number.
electricity.meterLocation: Each residence is separately metered; the meter number is on your lease rider.
electricity.costNote: These are real ranges for this building because heat and cooling are not on your meter — you are paying for lights, outlets, the washer and dryer, and the fan coil's fan. July and August run at the top of the range.

internet.bulkNote: There is no bulk internet deal and no mandatory building provider, so you pick and you pay your provider directly.
internet.typicalCost: Fios 500/500 runs about $75 a month and gigabit about $95. Spectrum starts around $70.
internet.installation: Both providers are already in the building, so activation is usually a self-install kit or a one-hour appointment. Installers file a certificate of insurance and work Monday through Friday 9:00am - 5:00pm.
internet.amenityWifi: The resident network in the amenity spaces is 'Larkin Resident'; the password is in the resident app and rotates each quarter. There is a separate guest network in the lobby.

wifiAndUtilities.television: Fios TV and Spectrum both serve the building. Satellite dishes are not permitted on terraces, balconies, or the facade.
wifiAndUtilities.waterAndGas: Water, sewer, and cooking gas are master metered and included. There is no separate water bill and no National Grid account for a resident to open.
wifiAndUtilities.residentSummary: Heat, hot water, cooling, water, cooking gas, and trash are included in your rent, and so is the WiFi in every amenity space. What you pay separately is electricity through Con Edison and internet in your own residence. Because heat and cooling come off the building's central system rather than your meter, the electric bill is small — figure $45 to $70 in a studio and $95 to $160 in a three-bedroom, with July and August at the top. The building is wired for both Verizon Fios and Spectrum with no bulk contract, so you choose. Open the Con Edison account at least three business days before you pick up keys, because the desk cannot release them without the account number.

packages.room: The Package Room, behind the lobby
packages.lockers: Luxer lockers, 24 hours, opened with your fob or the code in the app

coldStorage.type: Two refrigerated lockers and one freezer locker
coldStorage.holdTime: 24 hours. Grocery and meal deliveries are put in cold storage automatically when the carrier marks them perishable.
coldStorage.note: The desk texts you the moment something goes into cold storage, and it stays yours for 24 hours before staff has to clear it.

packages.notification: A text and an email the minute an item is logged in, with the carrier and the locker number.

holdingPeriod.lockers: 10 days, then the item goes back to the carrier
holdingPeriod.oversized: 10 days at the desk, same as a locker
holdingPeriod.feeNote: There is no daily storage fee. Items are returned to the carrier on day 11 rather than charged for.

oversizedItems.definition: Anything that does not fit a Luxer locker, roughly larger than 24 by 20 by 15 inches or heavier than 50 pounds
oversizedItems.handling: Held at the front desk, which is staffed 24 hours. Furniture and appliances are treated as a delivery and go through the service entrance on 5th Street during business hours.
oversizedItems.deskHours: The desk handles oversized items, cold storage, and dry cleaning drop-off 8:00am - 10:00pm daily. Lockers are always available.

notAccepted: Anything requiring an adult signature or ID at delivery
Items with a declared value over $2,500
Perishables that need a freezer beyond 24 hours
packages.outbound: Leave a labeled prepaid package with the desk for UPS, FedEx, or USPS pickup, or use the Luxer return slot. The desk does not print labels.
packages.mail: USPS boxes are in the mail room off the lobby, keyed separately from your fob. Package mail from USPS goes into the same Luxer lockers.
packages.vacationHold: Tell the desk and they will hold everything for up to 14 days without the 10-day clock running.
packages.foodDelivery: Food and grocery couriers come to the lobby, not to your door, unless you have opted into door delivery in the resident app for the hours between 7:00am and 11:00pm.
packages.liability: Packages are accepted as a courtesy. The building logs every item in and out and the lobby is on camera, but it does not insure your deliveries — that is what renters insurance contents coverage is for.
packages.residentSummary: Luxer lockers behind the lobby are open 24 hours with your fob, and there is refrigerated and freezer storage for groceries. You get a text and an email the minute a package lands. Anything too big for a locker waits with the front desk, which is staffed around the clock, and everything is held for ten days before it goes back to the carrier — there is no storage fee. Cold storage holds for 24 hours. The desk cannot accept anything needing a signature, a COD, or an item declared over $2,500, and food couriers stop in the lobby unless you have turned on door delivery in the app.

buildingAccess.system: Encrypted fob plus a mobile credential in the resident app. The lobby is attended 24 hours and there is a live-in resident manager.

fobsPerResidence.note: Two fobs come with the residence. Additional fobs are $50 each, up to four, and every fob is tied to a named adult on the lease or a registered occupant.

fobOpens: Elevator to your floor and to floors 3, 4, and 34
buildingAccess.elevatorRestriction: Elevators are floor-restricted. Your fob calls your own floor and the three amenity floors, nothing else.
buildingAccess.lostFob: Report it immediately and the desk kills the credential on the spot. A killed fob cannot be revived; the replacement is $50.
buildingAccess.mobileCredential: The resident app opens the same doors over Bluetooth. It works on one phone at a time, and re-pairing a new phone is done at the desk with ID.
buildingAccess.visitorAccess: Guests are announced at the desk and held in the lobby until you answer, or they use the 24-hour QR pass you issue in the app, which opens the vestibule and the elevator to your floor only. The desk logs a photo ID for anyone going up without you.
buildingAccess.deliveryAccess: Carriers reach the lobby and the package room, never a residential floor. Furniture and appliance deliveries use the service entrance on 5th Street during business hours with the desk notified.
buildingAccess.contractorAccess: Anyone working in your residence is on the day's access list with a certificate of insurance on file, and works Monday through Friday 9:00am - 5:00pm.

lockout.procedure: Go to the front desk. Staff verifies you against the lease and a photo ID and lets you in — 24 hours, no appointment.
lockout.note: The first lockout in a lease year is free. After that it is $75, or $125 between 11:00pm and 7:00am when the resident manager has to come down. Charged to your ledger, never in cash at the desk.

buildingAccess.keyHoldProgram: The building does not keep a copy of your key unless you opt in. If you do, it lives in a sealed, numbered envelope in the manager's safe and is only opened for an emergency or for access you authorize in writing.
buildingAccess.staffEntry: Staff enter for scheduled work with at least 24 hours' written notice, and immediately without notice for a genuine emergency such as water, fire, or gas. Every entry is logged with the time and the reason.
buildingAccess.cameras: Cameras cover the lobby, the elevators, the amenity floors, the garage, the bike room, and the service entrance. Footage is retained 30 days and released only to law enforcement on a valid request. There are no cameras in any residence, corridor bathroom, or the Recovery Suite.
buildingAccess.doorRules: No door in the building gets propped, including the stair doors and the garage pedestrian door. Stairs are for exit and for exercise, not for access between floors.
buildingAccess.emergencies: Call 911 first. Then tell the front desk, which is staffed 24 hours and holds the FDNY key box and the elevator recall.
buildingAccess.residentSummary: Your fob opens the lobby, the elevator to your floor and the three amenity floors, and every amenity door, and the resident app does the same over Bluetooth. Two fobs come with the residence and a third or fourth is $50. Guests are announced at the desk or use a 24-hour QR pass you send from the app, and carriers get the lobby and the package room only. If you lock yourself out, the desk verifies you against the lease and lets you in — the first time in a lease year is free, after that it is $75, or $125 between 11:00pm and 7:00am.

smoking.scope: The entire property. Residences, terraces, balconies, corridors, stairwells, the garage, the bike room, every amenity floor and outdoor deck, and the sidewalk within 15 feet of any entrance.
coveredSubstances: Cannabis in any smoked or vaped form
smoking.cannabisNote: Adult-use cannabis is legal in New York, and the building's smoke-free policy still applies to it exactly as it applies to tobacco. Edibles are not a lease matter.
smoking.openFlame: No charcoal grills, no propane tanks, no fire pits, and no candles on any terrace or balcony. The gas grills and firepits on The Terrace are building equipment and are the only open flame permitted outdoors.
smoking.leaseRider: Every lease includes a signed smoke-free rider. Under New York City Local Law 147 of 2017, every building with three or more residences must have a written smoking policy and disclose it to residents; ours is the rider, and you get a copy at signing and again at every renewal.

violations.third: $500 and a notice to cure the lease
violations.damage: Smoke remediation — sealing, painting, replacing flooring — is billed at cost and is separate from any fine.

smoking.guests: The policy covers your guests, and the charge lands on your ledger.
smoking.howToReport: Tell the front desk with the time and where you smelled it. Staff can usually place a stack within a day or two.
smoking.residentSummary: The Larkin is smoke-free everywhere — inside your residence, on the terraces and balconies, in the garage and the bike room, on every amenity floor, and within fifteen feet of the entrance. That covers cigarettes, cigars, hookah, vaping, and cannabis, which is legal in New York and still not permitted here. No charcoal, no propane, and no candles outdoors; the gas grills on The Terrace are the exception. You sign a smoke-free rider with your lease, as New York City requires, and a violation runs from a written notice to $250 to $500 and a notice to cure.

noiseAndQuietHours.generalStandard: Outside quiet hours the standard is simple: nothing a neighbor can hear through a closed door.
noiseAndQuietHours.floorCovering: Your lease carries the standard New York clause — carpets or rugs covering at least 80 percent of the floor area in every room other than the kitchen, bathrooms, entry, and closets. It is the single biggest thing that keeps this building quiet.
amenityNoise: The Terrace deck goes quiet at 10:00pm and closes at 11:00pm
The Overlook sky terrace closes at 11:00pm year-round
No amplified music in any outdoor amenity space at any hour
The Reading Room on 34 is a no-calls, no-meetings room around the clock
noiseAndQuietHours.instruments: Acoustic practice is fine 9:00am - 9:00pm. Amplified instruments and drums are not, at any hour.
noiseAndQuietHours.residentWork: Alterations need written consent from management. Any approved contractor works Monday through Friday 9:00am - 5:00pm, never on a weekend, with a certificate of insurance on file.
noiseAndQuietHours.buildingWork: Scheduled building work runs Monday through Friday 8:00am - 5:00pm. The resident manager posts anything loud at least 48 hours ahead in the lobby and the app.
noiseAndQuietHours.howToReport: Call or visit the front desk while it is happening — that is what the 24-hour desk is for. The desk logs the time and the residence and the resident manager follows up in writing. For something the building cannot resolve, 311 handles the city noise code and 911 handles anything unsafe.
noiseAndQuietHours.escalation: A first substantiated complaint is a conversation. A second in six months is a written notice. A third is a notice to cure the lease.
noiseAndQuietHours.confidentiality: The neighbor you complain about is told the time and the nature of the noise, never who reported it.
noiseAndQuietHours.residentSummary: Quiet hours are 10:00pm to 8:00am Sunday through Thursday and 11:00pm to 9:00am Friday and Saturday, and the rest of the day the standard is nothing a neighbor hears through a closed door. Your lease requires rugs over 80 percent of the floor in every room but the kitchen, baths, entry, and closets, which is what actually keeps a tower this size quiet. Outdoor amenity spaces have no amplified music at any hour and go quiet at 10:00pm. Report noise to the front desk while it is happening — it is staffed 24 hours, it logs the time, and it never tells your neighbor who called.

shortTermRentals.legalBasis: A rental of fewer than 30 days in a Class A multiple dwelling where the permanent resident is not present is illegal under New York Multiple Dwelling Law 4(8)(a). Since New York City's Local Law 18 took effect in September 2023, hosts also have to register with the Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement, and The Larkin is on the city's prohibited buildings list, so no registration can be issued here.
shortTermRentals.enforcement: A first listing is a $1,000 charge and a notice to cure. A second is a termination of the lease. The building also cooperates with OSE, which fines the host directly.
shortTermRentals.whyItMatters: It is not a house preference. A short-term guest invalidates the building's insurance and the certificate of occupancy, and the fines land on the owner.

subletting.conditions: With written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld — that is your right under New York Real Property Law 226-b in a building with four or more residences.
subletting.howToRequest: Send a written request by certified mail, return receipt requested, to Halbrook Residential Management at the building address, at least 30 days before the sublet would start.
requestMustInclude: The term of the sublet, with start and end dates
The name, home address, and business address of the proposed subtenant
The written consent of any co-tenant or guarantor
A copy of the proposed sublease with a copy of your lease attached
subletting.landlordResponse: Management has 10 days to ask for additional information and 30 days from your request, or from the additional information, to consent or to state the reasons for refusal in writing. No answer within 30 days is a consent.
subletting.screening: The proposed subtenant completes the same application as any resident. The application fee is $20 per adult, the New York cap.
subletting.termLimits: A sublet cannot run longer than your remaining lease term, and you stay liable for the rent and for the residence the whole time.
subletting.amenityAccess: An approved subtenant gets fobs and full amenity access. Your fobs are deactivated for the sublet term.

sublettingAndShortTermRentals.assignment: Assigning the lease outright requires management's written consent, which may be withheld — that is the distinction Real Property Law 226-b draws between an assignment and a sublet. If consent is refused, you may be released from the lease on 30 days' notice.
sublettingAndShortTermRentals.roommates: New York Real Property Law 235-f lets you add one additional occupant plus that occupant's dependent children beyond the named tenants and immediate family. Tell the resident manager within 30 days so the person is on the access list. Adding a roommate to the lease itself requires the same application and income review.

earlyTermination.notice: Sixty days' written notice, to the resident manager in writing or to residents@thelarkinlic.com.
earlyTermination.feeNote: There is no early termination fee and no two-month buyout. A flat liquidated sum is not enforceable in New York, because Real Property Law 227-e measures what you owe by the owner's actual damages after reasonable efforts to re-rent.
earlyTermination.liability: You stay responsible for the rent until the residence is re-rented. That liability ends the day a new lease begins, and it never exceeds the rent that would have come due through the end of your term.
earlyTermination.dutyToMitigate: Real Property Law 227-e requires the owner to make reasonable efforts to re-rent. Ownership markets the residence immediately, on the same terms, and any rent collected from a new resident reduces what you owe.
earlyTermination.securityDeposit: Returned on the normal schedule, within 14 days of move-out with an itemized statement, if the residence is in good order.
earlyTermination.militaryAndSafety: Servicemembers may terminate under the federal Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, and victims of domestic violence may terminate under Real Property Law 227-c. Neither carries a fee. Those requests go to the resident manager.

sublettingAndShortTermRentals.corporateLeases: Considered on a 12-month minimum, with the company as tenant, a named occupant on the lease, and a certificate of insurance. Rotating occupants are not permitted.
sublettingAndShortTermRentals.residentSummary: Short-term rentals are not permitted here in any form. A rental under thirty days without you present is illegal under state law, the building is on New York City's prohibited buildings list under Local Law 18, and a listing costs $1,000 and a notice to cure the first time. Subletting is different and it is allowed: send a written request by certified mail thirty days out with the term, the subtenant's name and addresses, your reason, and where you will be living, and management answers in writing within thirty days. There is a $250 administrative fee and the subtenant applies like anyone else at $20 an adult. You stay on the lease and stay liable for the term.

insurance.who: Every residence, maintained for the entire lease term including renewals.
insurance.contentsCoverage: Your call on the amount. Most residents here carry $25,000 to $50,000.
insurance.waterDamageLegalLiability: Included in the required liability coverage. Ask your carrier to confirm the policy covers water damage you cause to other residences.
insurance.additionalInterest: 5-08 46th Avenue Owner LLC, c/o Halbrook Residential Management, 5-08 46th Avenue, Long Island City, NY 11101
insurance.proofDue: Before key pickup. The desk cannot release keys without a certificate on file.
insurance.renewalProof: A new certificate every time the policy renews. The app sends a reminder 30 days out.

lapse.consequence: If coverage lapses, the building may place a landlord liability policy that protects the owner and not you, and bill it to your ledger at $14.95 a month until you provide proof of your own.
lapse.note: That placed policy covers the building's interest only. It does nothing for your belongings.

insurance.petLiability: If you have a dog, the policy's liability coverage cannot exclude the breed. Bring that page with the pet registration.
insurance.typicalCost: $15 to $30 a month for a studio or one-bedroom in Long Island City, more with high-value contents or jewelry riders.
insurance.moversAndContractors: Separate from your policy. Any mover, installer, or contractor files a certificate of insurance naming the owner and the manager as additional insureds — see the moving policy for the limits.
insurance.floodNote: Parts of Hunters Point sit in a FEMA flood zone. The Larkin's residences start on the fifth floor and the mechanical plant is above the design flood elevation, so residential flood exposure is low; contents flood coverage is still your decision.
insurance.residentSummary: Renters insurance is required for the whole lease term, with at least $300,000 in personal liability, and the certificate has to be on file before the desk hands you keys. Name 5-08 46th Avenue Owner LLC, care of Halbrook Residential Management at the building address, as additional interest. Coverage in this neighborhood runs about $15 to $30 a month. If it lapses, the building can place a policy that protects the owner and not your belongings and bill you $14.95 a month for it, so keep the certificate current — the app reminds you thirty days ahead. If you have a dog, make sure the liability coverage does not exclude the breed.

applicationFee.basis: New York caps application fees at $20 per applicant, and that has to cover the background and credit check. The cap came in with the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019.
applicationFee.receipt: You get a copy of the background and credit report and a receipt for the fee, which the law requires.

brokerFee.note: There is no broker fee. The Larkin is leased in-house by the Halbrook Residential team, so nobody hires a broker on your behalf. Under New York City's FARE Act, in effect since June 2025, the party who hires the broker pays the broker.

securityDeposit.cap: One month is the statutory maximum in New York under General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a). No last month's rent, no additional security for a pet or a lower credit score.
securityDeposit.heldIn: An interest-bearing account at a New York bank, as required for buildings with six or more residences. The bank and account are disclosed at signing, interest is credited to you annually, and the owner retains the 1 percent administrative fee the statute allows.
securityDeposit.return: Within 14 days of move-out, with an itemized statement of any deduction. Failure to itemize forfeits the right to keep any of it.
securityDeposit.preMoveOutInspection: You are offered a walkthrough between 14 and 30 days before your lease ends, with a written list of anything that would be deducted, so you can fix it first. That offer is a legal requirement, not a courtesy.

incomeRequirement.basis: Annual gross household income of at least 40 times the monthly rent. Roommates may combine incomes.
incomeRequirement.example: Multiply the monthly rent of the residence you are applying for by 40. That is the annual gross household income we look for, and roommates may combine incomes to reach it. The leasing team runs the number against the live rent for that residence; no rent figure lives in this document.

guarantor.residency: Must reside in New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, or Pennsylvania
guarantor.documents: Same document package as an applicant, plus the guarantor signs the lease and a guaranty rider
guarantor.institutional: Third-party guarantor services such as TheGuarantors and Insurent are accepted and are the usual path for an applicant who is short on income or has no US credit history.

credit.target: 700 or above for a standard approval
credit.below700: An application under 700 is approved with a guarantor or an institutional guaranty rather than with extra money down, because New York does not allow a larger deposit.
credit.noCreditHistory: International applicants and recent graduates without US credit are common here. The usual path is an institutional guaranty or verified assets.

documentsRequired: Government-issued photo ID for each applicant
Letter of employment on company letterhead with title, salary, and start date
First two pages of last year's federal tax return
Contact information for your current landlord
documentsSelfEmployed: Two years of federal tax returns
A letter from your accountant confirming income
Three most recent months of bank statements
applicationRequirements.verification: Employment is verified directly. Prior landlord is contacted for payment history.

criminalHistory.basis: The New York City Fair Chance for Housing Act, effective January 1, 2025, took criminal history out of housing screening. We do not ask about it on the application and it is not part of the decision, apart from the narrow state sex offender registry check the law still permits after a conditional offer.

housingCourtHistory.basis: New York law since 2019 bars refusing an applicant solely because they were once in housing court. We do not buy or use tenant blacklist data.

applicationRequirements.sourceOfIncome: Housing vouchers and rental assistance, including CityFHEPS and Section 8, are a lawful source of income in New York City and are accepted. Refusing them is illegal, and the voucher counts toward the income requirement.
applicationRequirements.occupancyStandard: Set by the New York City Housing Maintenance Code and the certificate of occupancy, not by a house rule. Questions about who may live in a residence go to the resident manager.
applicationRequirements.decisionTimeline: One to three business days once the file is complete.

holdDeposit.policy: There is no hold deposit. A signed application takes the residence off the market while we review it, and the building holds no money of yours before you sign a lease.
holdDeposit.basis: New York permits a $20 application fee and a security deposit of one month's rent, and essentially nothing else. General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(a) caps what an owner may hold and Real Property Law 238-a bars fees outside a short enumerated list, so a pre-lease advance that could be forfeited is not permitted.
holdDeposit.atSigning: The first month's rent and the one-month security deposit are due at lease signing. Nothing is due before it, and nothing you pay is forfeitable.

applicationRequirements.approvalWindow: An approval holds the residence for 48 hours. Leases are signed electronically and the first month's rent and the deposit are due at signing.
applicationRequirements.escalationNote: Whether a specific applicant qualifies, why an application was declined, and any request for an accommodation are never answered by the assistant. They go to the resident manager.
applicationRequirements.residentSummary: The application fee is $20 per adult, which is the New York cap, and it covers the credit and background check — you get a copy of both. There is no broker fee, because we lease in-house. Nothing is due before you sign. There is no hold deposit, and the first month's rent and the security deposit are collected at lease signing. The security deposit is one month's rent and cannot be more than that under state law, and it sits in an interest-bearing account with the bank disclosed to you at signing. We look for household income of 40 times the monthly rent, or a guarantor at 80 times who lives in New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, or Pennsylvania, and institutional guarantors are accepted. Bring photo ID, an employment letter, two pay stubs, last year's tax return, and two bank statements. We do not ask about criminal history, we do not use housing court records, and housing vouchers are accepted. Decisions take one to three business days.

leaseTerms.escalationNote: The legal regulated rent for a particular residence, the rent registration history, how the 421-a benefit applies to a specific tenancy, and any question about a rent overcharge go to the resident manager. The assistant does not answer them, and it does not quote a rent from this file.
leaseTerms.standardRange: One year or two years, at your choice. Rent stabilization sets those two options, and the owner cannot refuse either one.
leaseTerms.startDates: Any calendar day. A mid-month start is prorated on the actual days.

lateFee.trigger: Charged only after rent is more than 5 days late
lateFee.basis: New York caps late fees at $50 or 5 percent of the monthly rent, whichever is less, and only after a 5-day grace period.

leaseTerms.paymentMethods: ACH from the resident portal at no charge, or a card for a 2.95 percent processing fee. No cash, and the front desk does not take rent.
leaseTerms.regulatoryStatus: All 318 residences are rent stabilized for the term of the building's 421-a benefit, and that includes the 222 market-rate homes. Under RPTL 421-a(16) the tax benefit stabilizes every residence in the building for the whole 35-year exemption period, and the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act of 2019 ended high-rent deregulation, so a residence does not leave stabilization by crossing a rent threshold. The rent on your lease is a legal regulated rent registered with DHCR, and where the rent you actually pay is lower the lease carries a preferential rent rider stating both figures. Renewals are offered on DHCR form RTP-8 at one year or two years, at the increase the New York City Rent Guidelines Board has ordered for a lease beginning on your renewal date, served 90 to 150 days before your lease ends with 60 days to accept. The 96 income-restricted residences are the Option C set-aside at 130 percent of area median income; they were leased through NYC Housing Connect and are administered by the city's designated marketing agent, outside the leasing office.
leaseTerms.regulatoryStatusNote: Corrected 2026-09-07. This field previously read that the market-rate residences were free-market and neither rent stabilized nor rent controlled, which was wrong under 421-a(16), and it carried a residence count that no longer matches property.json. Counsel reviews the corrected language before it is quoted to a caller; until then a stabilization question goes to the resident manager.
leaseTerms.guarantorRider: A guarantor signs the lease and a separate guaranty rider covering the initial term and any renewal.
leaseTerms.utilitiesRider: Confirms what is included — heat, hot water, cooling, water, cooking gas — and that electricity and internet are yours.
otherRiders: DHCR Rider for Rent Stabilized Tenants, required with every vacancy lease and every renewal
421-a rider disclosing the tax benefit and the rent stabilization that comes with it
Preferential rent rider where the rent you pay is below the legal regulated rent
Smoke-free rider, required by NYC Local Law 147
Window guard rider, required by the NYC Health Code for any residence with a child under 11
Bedbug disclosure, required annually by New York State
Lead paint disclosure, which reads not applicable in a 2023 building
leaseTerms.renewalNoticeLaw: Renewals here follow the Rent Stabilization Code, not the market-rate notice rule. Section 2523.5 requires the owner to serve a renewal offer on DHCR form RTP-8 between 90 and 150 days before your lease ends, and you have 60 days to accept and to choose a one-year or two-year term. Real Property Law 226-c, the 30, 60, and 90-day notice rule, governs unregulated tenancies and does not displace that here.
leaseTerms.residentSummary: Leases here run one year or two years, and the term is your choice. Every residence in the building is rent stabilized for the term of the 421-a benefit, market-rate homes included, so the rent on your lease is a legal regulated rent and your renewal arrives on DHCR form RTP-8 at the Rent Guidelines Board increase, served 90 to 150 days before your lease ends with 60 days to accept. Rent is due on the first, the late fee is $50 and only after five days, which is the state cap, and you pay by ACH from the portal at no charge. Your lease carries the DHCR rent stabilization rider, the smoke-free rider, and a preferential rent rider if the rent you pay is below the legal regulated rent. Advertised rents and any concession come from the leasing team against live availability, never from this document.

pricing.note: Pricing is never answered from this file. Rents, concessions, and availability live in the inventory feed and are quoted by the leasing team against live data. No rent figure and no residence number belongs in this document, which is reviewed once a year and outlives every price in it.
pricing.pricingByTerm: Each term available on a residence is priced separately. The actual rent for a term, and whether a concession is running on it, come from the inventory feed.

concession.current: Stated on the residence in the inventory feed, never here.
concession.expiryHandling: A concession carries its own expiration date on the residence record. This document does not restate it, because a date frozen in a policy file outlives the offer it describes.
concession.howApplied: A free month is taken as the first full month of the lease. It is not amortized across the term.
concession.structure: Every residence here is rent stabilized, so a concession is written against the legal regulated rent rather than reducing it. Where the rent you actually pay stays below that figure, the lease carries a preferential rent rider stating both numbers.
concession.brokerFee: None. The Larkin is leased in-house.

netEffectiveExplanation.rule: Advertised rents are net effective and reflect the concession. The gross rent is the legal regulated rent printed on the lease, and it is the number every renewal increase is calculated from. It is the higher of the two.
netEffectiveExplanation.math: Net effective = gross rent multiplied by the number of months you pay, divided by the number of months in the term.
netEffectiveExplanation.example: On a twelve-month lease with one month free, the net effective rent is the gross rent times eleven, divided by twelve. Ask the leasing team for both figures on the residence you are considering; both come from live inventory.
netEffectiveExplanation.disclosureRule: The leasing team states both numbers before being asked. Never quote the net effective figure alone.

pricing.shortTerms: Not offered. A rent stabilized lease runs one year or two years at your choice, so there is no short term to price and no short-term premium to quote.

renewal.offerTiming: The renewal offer comes on DHCR form RTP-8, served between 90 and 150 days before your lease ends, by mail or personal delivery, with a copy by email and on paper under your door.
renewal.responseWindow: Sixty days to accept, running from the date the offer is served. The renewal takes effect on the later of your lease expiration date or 90 days after the offer is served. The terms are not requoted at market if you take the full window, because the increase is set by the Rent Guidelines Board and not by the leasing office.
renewal.termsOffered: One year or two years. You choose the term and the owner cannot refuse either one.
renewal.increaseBasis: The New York City Rent Guidelines Board order in effect for a lease beginning on your renewal date, applied to your legal regulated rent. The offer states the current legal regulated rent, the ordered percentage for the one-year and the two-year term, and the resulting rent for each. It is not set against market rents for the line or the floor band, and it is not negotiable.
renewal.statutoryNotice: Rent Stabilization Code section 2523.5 governs this building: the RTP-8 offer is served 90 to 150 days before the lease ends and you have 60 days to accept. Real Property Law 226-c, the 30, 60, and 90-day rule, applies to unregulated tenancies and does not govern a renewal here.
renewal.newApplication: None. No new application, no new fee, no new credit check.
renewal.securityDeposit: Rides over untouched. New York does not permit topping it up when the rent goes up, because one month is the cap in the first place.
renewal.concessionsAtRenewal: A renewal concession is a separate decision and is never guaranteed. If one is offered it is stated on the renewal notice, not assumed from the original lease.
renewal.monthToMonth: Not available. A rent stabilized tenancy does not convert to month-to-month, and there is no 110 percent holdover rate. The owner must offer a one-year or two-year renewal at the Rent Guidelines Board increase, and until you sign one the terms of your existing lease continue.
renewal.holdover: If you stay past the end of your lease without returning a signed renewal, the terms of your existing lease continue and the owner's remedy is a proceeding under the Rent Stabilization Code, not a higher rate. Accepting rent does not create a month-to-month tenancy in a stabilized residence.

transfers.eligibility: After 9 months of residency and a clean payment history
transfers.term: A new lease of at least 12 months on the new residence
transfers.deposit: Your existing deposit transfers. There is no second deposit.
transfers.conditions: Subject to availability, and the transfer date follows the new residence's availability, not your convenience. The freight elevator is reserved the same way as any move.

renewal.notToRenew: Sixty days' written notice if you are not renewing, which is also what your lease requires. Notice goes to residents@thelarkinlic.com or to the resident manager in writing.
moveOutProcess: Accept the pre-move-out inspection offered 14 to 30 days before the end of the lease and get the written punch list
Reserve the freight elevator, Monday through Saturday 9:00am - 5:00pm, with the mover's certificate of insurance 5 business days ahead
Return every fob, garage remote, and mail key to the front desk
Deposit returned within 14 days with an itemized statement
renewal.escalationNote: A specific renewal rate, a ledger balance, or the status of a particular offer comes from the account system, not from this file.
renewal.residentSummary: Your renewal arrives on DHCR form RTP-8, served 90 to 150 days before your lease ends, and you have sixty days to accept. You pick one year or two years, and the increase is the one the New York City Rent Guidelines Board ordered for a lease starting on your renewal date, applied to your legal regulated rent. There is no renewal fee, no new application, and no new deposit. There is no month-to-month option and no holdover premium, because a stabilized lease does not convert. If you would rather move within the building, you can transfer after nine months with a $500 fee and no second deposit. If you are not renewing, sixty days' written notice, take the pre-move-out walkthrough we offer two to four weeks ahead, and the deposit comes back within fourteen days with an itemized statement.

storage.location: Cellar level, off the service corridor, fob access
storage.priceRange: $95 to $240 a month depending on size
storage.agreement: Month to month, separate from the lease, 30 days' notice either way
storage.waitlist: About six weeks. Ask the front desk or email residents@thelarkinlic.com to join.
prohibited: Anything flammable, including gasoline, propane, and lithium batteries being charged
storage.insurance: Contents are yours to insure. Your renters policy usually extends to a storage locker on the same property, but confirm it with your carrier.
storage.residentSummary: Private storage in the cellar starts at $95 a month for a 4-by-4-by-6 locker and runs to $240 for the largest, on a month-to-month agreement with thirty days' notice. Access is 24 hours with your fob. There is a waitlist of about six weeks right now. Nothing flammable, perishable, or alive goes in a locker, and the contents are covered by your renters policy, not by the building.

feeSchedule.residentSummary: The charges that exist here are short: $20 an adult to apply and one month's security, and that is everything due before you have keys. There is no broker fee, no hold deposit, no pet fee, no move-in or move-out deposit, and no amenity deposit, because New York caps what a building may hold to one month's rent. Parking is $425 a month with EV charging included, storage starts at $95, and the bike room, the amenity spaces, and pet rent are all zero. Everything posts to your resident ledger, the late fee is $50 and only after five days, and the front desk does not take money for anything. Damage is billed at cost after the fact with an itemized statement, never collected up front.
feeSchedule.capNote: General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(a) caps everything the owner may hold to one month's rent as security, and Real Property Law 238-a bars fees outside a short enumerated list. That is why the hold deposit, the pet fee, the move-in and move-out deposits, the amenity deposits, and the early termination fee are gone from this schedule. It is the statute, not a house courtesy.
